field: Reliable LLM-assisted diagnostic knowledge graph authoring

reports.title: Extract, Define, Canonicalize: An LLM-based Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction

sections.problem: Large or unavailable schemas make direct schema-conditioned extraction difficult.
sections.gap: Prior prompting approaches do not scale cleanly to large schemas.
sections.coreIdea: Extract openly, define relation semantics, then canonicalize to a schema.
sections.method: Three phases plus retrieval of schema elements relevant to the current text.
sections.evidence: Evaluation on three KGC benchmarks reports high-quality triples with larger schemas.
sections.limitation: Targets factual triples rather than diagnostic educational constructs.
sections.inspiration: Perform local concept discovery before explicit global canonicalization.

reports.title: SPIRES: Structured Prompt Interrogation and Recursive Extraction of Semantics
reports.authors: J. Harry Caufield; Harshad Hegde; Vincent Emonet; Nomi L. Harris; Marcin P. Joachimiak; Nicolas Matentzoglu; HyeongSik Kim; Sierra A. T. Moxon; Justin T. Reese; Melissa A. Haendel; Peter N. Robinson; Christopher J. Mungall

sections.problem: Free-form output is difficult to validate and align with ontologies.
sections.gap: Prompt-only extraction lacks typed domain contracts.
sections.coreIdea: Use LinkML schemas to drive recursive extraction and ontology grounding.
sections.method: Schema-guided structured prompting followed by term grounding.
sections.evidence: Demonstrates reusable schema-conformant biomedical extraction workflows.
sections.limitation: Schema compliance does not establish pedagogical or source validity.
sections.inspiration: Require typed stage outputs and distinguish structural from semantic validation.

reports.title: PiVe: Prompting with Iterative Verification Improving Graph-based Generative Capability of LLMs
reports.authors: Jiuzhou Han; Nigel Collier; Wray Buntine; Ehsan Shareghi

sections.problem: LLMs omit or corrupt elements of generated graph structures.
sections.gap: A generator often lacks precise feedback about its structured errors.
sections.coreIdea: A smaller independent verifier supplies fine-grained corrective instructions.
sections.method: Iterative online or offline generator--verifier correction.
sections.evidence: Consistent improvements are reported on three graph-generation datasets.
sections.limitation: Its error focus does not cover all grounding and granularity failures.
sections.inspiration: Add a bounded verifier with KnowAct-specific error labels and source context.

reports.title: SAC-KG: Exploiting Large Language Models as Skilled Automatic Constructors for Domain Knowledge Graph

sections.problem: Domain KG construction needs dependable precision at large scale.
sections.gap: Manual intervention limits scale while naive generation propagates errors.
sections.coreIdea: Separate Generator, Verifier, and Pruner roles during iterative expansion.
sections.method: Entity-centered multi-level graph expansion with verification and pruning.
sections.evidence: Reports a million-node graph and 89.32 percent sampled precision.
sections.limitation: Recall is difficult to establish and the task is not a bounded curriculum graph.
sections.inspiration: Use proposer--verifier separation, plus a coverage pass and quarantine.

reports.title: KGGen: Extracting Knowledge Graphs from Plain Text with Language Models

sections.problem: Aliases and related forms make automatically extracted graphs sparse.
sections.gap: Existing extractors retain redundant entities and relations.
sections.coreIdea: Separate extraction passes and iteratively cluster entities and relations.
sections.method: Language-model extraction with entity resolution and the MINE evaluation benchmark.
sections.evidence: Reports competitive retrieval and improved concision and information retention.
sections.limitation: Entity concision is not equivalent to diagnostic concept granularity.
sections.inspiration: Retrieve merge candidates, then adjudicate keep, alias, merge, or split.

reports.title: KARMA: Leveraging Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Knowledge Graph Enrichment

sections.problem: Scientific KGs require extraction, integration, conflict resolution, and provenance.
sections.gap: Single-stage systems struggle across the entire lifecycle.
sections.coreIdea: Coordinate specialized agents for different construction responsibilities.
sections.method: A nine-agent pipeline over scientific literature.
sections.evidence: Reports large-scale PubMed enrichment and conflict reduction.
sections.limitation: LLM-based judging and no causal test that nine agents are necessary.
sections.inspiration: Use role specialization only where it creates a checkable boundary.

reports.title: Can LLMs be Good Graph Judge for Knowledge Graph Construction?

sections.problem: Noise, domain specificity, and hallucination reduce generated-KG precision.
sections.gap: Direct extraction lacks a robust post-generation quality gate.
sections.coreIdea: Entity-centric denoising followed by a trained LLM graph judge.
sections.method: Denoise input context, extract triples, and classify their quality.
sections.evidence: Evaluates two general and one domain-specific text--graph dataset.
sections.limitation: Binary filtering can sacrifice coverage and inherit judge bias.
sections.inspiration: Measure judge calibration and add typed repair instead of deletion alone.

reports.title: LLMs as Knowledge Graph Refiners: Mitigating Factual Inconsistencies in Generative Knowledge Extraction

sections.problem: Generated triples exhibit factual and representational inconsistencies.
sections.coreIdea: Choose an error-specific delete, edit, or rewrite action.
sections.method: Human-derived error taxonomy and a fine-tuned triple refiner.
sections.evidence: Reports broader quality gains across generative extractors.
sections.limitation: Triple-level factual repair omits diagnostic and graph-level validity.
sections.inspiration: Use keep, fix, rewrite, delete, and quarantine with independent approval.

sections.problem: Autoregressive extraction may generate objects outside a fixed KG schema.
sections.gap: Unconstrained decoding does not guarantee valid entities and relations.
sections.coreIdea: Constrain generation with entity and relation tries.
sections.evidence: Demonstrates competitive closed extraction on established datasets.
sections.limitation: Fixed schemas are unsuitable for initial concept discovery.
sections.inspiration: Enforce hard graph contracts after open candidate discovery.

reports.title: GoLLIE: Annotation Guidelines Improve Zero-Shot Information-Extraction

sections.problem: IE systems generalize poorly to unseen schemas and nuanced labels.
sections.gap: Label names alone under-specify annotation decisions.
sections.coreIdea: Condition extraction on detailed natural-language guidelines.
sections.method: Code-like schema descriptions and annotation instructions for zero-shot IE.
sections.evidence: Evaluates generalization across a broad collection of IE datasets.
sections.limitation: Guideline adherence does not ensure source or ontology validity.
sections.inspiration: Provide positive examples, near misses, and boundary rules for all labels.

reports.title: ACE: AI-Assisted Construction of Educational Knowledge Graphs with Prerequisite Relations

sections.problem: Experts cannot label all prerequisite pairs in a concept inventory.
sections.gap: Quadratic pair review makes educational KG authoring expensive.
sections.coreIdea: Rank candidate pairs for expert decisions and exploit graph inference.
sections.method: Embedding-based scoring, iterative expert labeling, and dynamic graph updates.
sections.evidence: Reports accurate graphs, reduced review effort, and a learner outcome study.
sections.limitation: Assumes concepts already exist and uses its own prerequisite semantics.
sections.inspiration: Prioritize expert review while keeping direct and inferred edges distinct.

reports.title: A Brief Introduction to Evidence-Centered Design
reports.authors: Robert J. Mislevy; Russell G. Almond; Janice F. Lukas

sections.problem: Assessment needs an explicit argument from observations to competence claims.
sections.gap: Tasks and scores are often designed without a coherent evidence model.
sections.coreIdea: Coordinate student, evidence, and task models.
sections.method: An assessment-design framework linking claims, observations, and elicitation tasks.
sections.evidence: A foundational conceptual and applied assessment framework.
sections.limitation: It is not a text-to-KG extraction algorithm.
sections.inspiration: Validate mastery rubrics and diagnostic questions as measurement artifacts.

reports.title: The Role of Competency Questions in Enterprise Engineering

sections.problem: Ontologies are hard to scope and evaluate when intended uses are implicit.
sections.gap: A representation can grow without a testable requirement boundary.
sections.coreIdea: Define competency questions the ontology must answer.
sections.method: Use questions to drive ontology axioms and benchmark adequacy.
sections.evidence: Foundational ontology-engineering method illustrated in enterprise modeling.
sections.limitation: Question design still requires domain judgment.
sections.inspiration: Freeze KnowAct graph requirements before LLM extraction.
